# State names

R has built-in vectors with the names of all 50 states in the U.S.

```{r}
state.name
```

## Exercise 1

Run each line below and add comments to the code to indicate what each line is doing.

```{r}
str_which(state.name,"V")
str_subset(state.name,"V")
str_subset(str_to_upper(state.name),"V")
str_subset(state.name,"[Vv]")
```

# Babynames

The `babynames` data contain U.S. baby name counts from the Social Security Administration, 1880–2017. A name is included if it occurs at least 5 times in a year.

**Each row is a name × sex × year combination, not one baby.** `n` is the number of babies with that name, and `prop` is `n` divided by the total number of babies of that sex born that year. Keep this in mind for every question below.

```{r}
glimpse(babynames)
```
